data.title: Boston Scientific restoring shipping after cyberattack
data.description:
Boston Scientific (BSX) traded higher on Friday after the cardiac device maker said it has begun restoring shipping capabilities for most of its products across its major distribution centers worldwide after a recent cybersecurity incident.

Shares of the Marlborough, Massachusetts-based MedTech fell last week after the company disclosed that a cybersecurity incident had affected some of its IT systems and disrupted its worldwide operations.

With assistance from CrowdStrike (CRWD) and other outside experts, Boston Scientific (BSX) said that it is becoming increasingly confident that unauthorized access was restricted to only some of its internal-facing IT infrastructure.

“As capabilities are validated and brought back online, we are progressively moving customer orders through the fulfillment process,” the company said in a statement after the close, adding that it will take some time for it to clear the current backlog.

“We are working expeditiously to restore shipping capabilities for additional products and locations as validation is completed and will continue to work to ramp up to full capacity,” Boston Scientific (BSX) noted.

TD Cowen welcomed the update, with analyst Joshua Jennings viewing “yesterday’s news as a big step forward for the company, and I think that today’s stock reaction fails to reflect this progress.” Jennings has a Buy rating and a $56 target on the stock.

data.title: Trump administration working on post-war Middle East strategy - report
data.description:
The Trump administration has started crafting a sweeping post-war strategy for the Middle East, intended to reshape U.S. engagement in the region once the Iran conflict concludes, according to a media report on Friday.

The framework, still in early development, is taking shape across both senior political levels and multiple agencies, Axios reported, citing two U.S. officials and two other sources with knowledge of the matter.

Three main pillars have reportedly emerged: building a U.S.-guaranteed regional alignment among allies to contain Tehran; securing broader regional stability by advancing the next phase of President Trump's Gaza plan, reaching a security agreement between Israel and Syria, and implementing the Israel-Lebanon agreement; and expanding the Abraham Accords toward the ultimate goal of Saudi-Israeli normalization.

The planning unfolds against a tight political calendar, with Israel's Oct. 27 elections and U.S. midterms in November looming over deliberations.

Trump has held two meetings with senior advisers in recent weeks to discuss the plan and privately told associates he's working on "something much bigger" in the Middle East after the Iran war, which is now in its sixth month, sources told Axios.

Administration officials stressed Trump intends to push forward regardless of Israeli election results—even if they produce a political stalemate.

Dear readers: We recognize that politics often intersects with the financial news of the day, so we invite you to click here to join the separate political discussion.

data.title: 3M stock losing its footing: What's behind the 4% weekly decline?
data.description:
3M (MMM) stock has extended its decline this week, falling roughly 4% from the ~$175 area to around $167.92 on Friday.

The decline has pushed the stock deeper into a short-term downtrend, with investors weighing ongoing PFAS-related risks alongside broader market and company-specific concerns.

A key overhang remains 3M’s exposure to PFAS litigation. A federal judge recently approved more than $2.5B of settlements involving 3M, DuPont (DD), Chemours (CC), and Corteva (CTVA) over pollution linked to “forever chemicals.”

While the ruling resolves part of the legal uncertainty, the companies continue to face other PFAS-related lawsuits, keeping litigation risk on investors’ radar.

The recent decline also came despite the company showing stronger operating momentum in its latest quarter. The company raised its full-year outlook, including EPS guidance to $8.80-$8.95 and free cash flow guidance to $4.7B-$4.9B.

However, management also flagged pressure across consumer electronics, auto, auto aftermarket, and U.S. consumer spending.

Technically, the picture has turned increasingly bearish. 3M stock has formed a series of lower highs and lower lows, while failed rebounds around the $170 area suggest buyers remain weak. 

RSI at 34.36 signals weak momentum, while a negative MACD adds to the bearish setup. Heavier volume during the selloff also points to increased selling pressure.

The weakness has left 3M stock trailing the broader market, with a 5.38% YTD gain versus 13.18% for the S&P 500 (SP500) and also recorded a 6.69% decline over the past month.

Wall Street and Quant remain bullish on the stock, with buy ratings of 3.77 and 4.18, respectively, while SA Analysts rate it Hold at 3.45. For now, $170 remains an important resistance zone to watch.

data.title: Nscale looking to raise $3.5B in new financing; Nvidia, Third Point may join: report
data.description:
U.K. artificial intelligence cloud computing firm Nscale is looking to raise $3.5B in new financing, with Nvidia (NVDA) and hedge fund Third Point likely participating, Bloomberg reported.

Nscale could sell as much as $1.5B in convertible notes, and Third Point, which is run by Dan Loeb, could lead the investment, the news outlet added, citing people familiar with the matter. Nvidia could help secure another $2B in funding, with the fundraising being led by Goldman Sachs (GS), Bloomberg added. 

Nscale, Nvidia, and Goldman Sachs did not immediately respond to a request for comment from Seeking Alpha.

Last month, it was reported that Nscale is looking to raise $3B in an initial public offering.

The company is developing data centers in sites including Norway and West Virginia and has told prospective investors it has around $51B of total contracted revenue ahead of the listing

Nscale announced plans to acquire Anyscale in July, a San Francisco-based software firm that scales AI workloads. The deal is reportedly valued at about $1.65B. The company is also planning to spend €695M (about $812M) on infrastructure in Portugal under an expansion of its collaboration with Microsoft (MSFT).

It was reported last month that Anthropic (ANTHRO) will pay Nscale $45B over several years in a deal for AI compute.

data.title: lululemon sinks to $100 support as momentum nears oversold levels
data.description:
Shares of lululemon athletica (LULU) suffered a brutal selloff during Friday afternoon trading, plunging some 17% to $100.70 per share to test critical support following the activewear giant's latest guidance cut and mounting international headwinds.

The massive gap-down leaves LULU shares down roughly 52% year-to-date, dragging the stock to price levels not seen since mid-2018. During the rout, the stock decisively breached a vital structural support zone around the $105 mark, a level that now acts as near-term overhead resistance. Shares are flirting with the psychologically important $100 per share threshold, a key battleground for bottom-fishers and short-sellers looking for the next major price action.

Momentum and trend indicators confirm a dominant shift to the downside. The breakdown violently ended a period of tight consolidation that had persisted since the beginning of August, during which the stock chopped back and forth between its 50-day and 100-day moving averages on the daily chart. Shares are now trading well below their 50-day, 100-day, and 200-day moving averages.

Furthermore, the relative strength index has plummeted to approximately 32, pushing the stock to the very edge of oversold territory, while the moving average convergence divergence, or MACD, indicator has officially registered a bearish crossover as selling pressure accelerated.

"Big Short" manager Michael Burry said earlier Friday that he would dip buy the stock if it fell below the $100 mark, noting that shares present a "fat pitch" at those levels despite affectionately referring to the stock as his portfolio's "trickster". The stock did briefly pierce that $100 floor during Friday morning's session, directly testing Burry's resolve as he navigates the elevated volatility.

data.title: Longer inflation stays high, harder it will be to bring it back down: Cleveland Fed's Hammack
data.description:
"Policy is not restrictive. Inflation is too high—and the longer it stays above our objective, the harder it will be to bring it back down," said Beth Hammack, president of the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland.

"Inflation is still above 3%. The labor market is stable and near my estimate of maximum employment. And businesses across the Fourth District tell me costs are rising and they're having to make tough choices," said the Federal Open Market Committee's voting member.

"Right now, what I'm hearing is that it's time to act," she said in a LinkedIn post.

Sharing an anecdote, she said a medium-sized manufacturer in Northeast Ohio told her that he thinks the FOMC should raise rates even though higher rates are bad for business. Because he's seen double-digit inflation in many of his input costs.

"Stories like his are emblematic of what I hear across the Fourth District and complement the hard data to paint a fuller picture of the economy," she noted.

data.title: Netflix hikes UK prices for the second time in 2026
data.description:
Netflix (NFLX) is raising the price of its streaming service in the UK beginning September 3, the second price hike this year.

A standard plan with ads will now cost 33.4% more at £7.99 ($10.81) per month; a standard tier with no ads is now 7.7% more at £13.99, and the price of the premium service is up 10.5% to £20.99.

The updated price tiers apply to new and existing customers. 

While Netflix (NFLX) says the higher prices are to “reflect improvements to our wide range of entertainment and the quality of our service,” UK subscribers might not be so willing to pay extra for the service with plenty of other free or more affordable options.

In October, VodafoneThree will launch Vodafone TV with free channels that come bundled with Netflix (NFLX) and HBO Max (WBD), while services like Disney+ (DIS), Discovery+ (WBD), and BritBox are all priced much more competitively than Netflix (NFLX).

Netflix (NFLX) shares are down more than 4% on Friday.

data.title: Anthropic’s efforts to build in-house payments tech could hurt Stripe: The Information
data.description:
Anthropic (ANTHRO) is looking to develop billing, fraud detection, and other financial infrastructure internally. The Information reported on Friday, citing its recent job postings, adding that the Claude maker’s in-house efforts could hurt Stripe (STRIP).

According to the job adverts, Anthropic's (ANTHRO) operations have become more complex due to its explosive topline growth, with its annualized revenue reaching nearly $45B  by May, a roughly fivefold jump in only five months. 

In an advert seeking a candidate who could overhaul its financial systems, including order management, provisioning, billing, and invoicing, the company said its “business is scaling faster than the processes and systems that support it.”

Its plans to internally build more payment infrastructure could give the AI startup more control over payment costs and help it reduce fees it pays to outside firms such as Stripe (STRIP).

The payment processor has in the past touted its relationship with Anthropic and highlighted its infrastructure for AI firms, noting that the company could meet the rising complexity of their payments.

However, it could take a long time for Anthropic (ANTHRO) to part ways with Stripe (STRIP) or other payment and billing vendors, and the job postings also don’t explicitly indicate that the company is preparing to cut its relationships with external processors.

Anthropic (ANTHRO) and Stripe (STRIP) didn’t immediately respond to requests for comment.

data.title: Quanex expects Q4 2026 revenue growth of 2% to 3% with 50 to 75 bps adjusted EBITDA margin expansion
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: Quanex Building Products (NX) Q3 2026

Management View

  • "Since then, the data has been mixed. On the new construction side of the market, activity has been weaker than we anticipated." (President, CEO & Chairman George Wilson)
  • "Permits have held up nicely... This means that builders are keeping their entitlement pipelines intact but are choosing not to break ground... it's why we continue to view the current market as being demand deferred rather than demand destroyed." (President, CEO & Chairman Wilson)
  • "We said then that we would implement targeted price increases in the mid-single digit to low teens range, phased in through the third quarter, and tailored by product line. And we have executed on that plan." (President, CEO & Chairman Wilson)
  • "As we now move into the optimization stage, we continue to advance strategic projects built around the 80-20 principle... designed to improve our customer performance, optimize our footprint and cost structure, and strengthen our margins." (President, CEO & Chairman Wilson)
  • "I'm very pleased with the work of our team in managing working capital, which enabled us to pay down debt and repurchase shares during the quarter." (President, CEO & Chairman Wilson)
  • "On a consolidated basis, we reported net sales of $501.8 million during the third quarter of 2026" and "we reported net income of $26.5 million, $0.58 per diluted share" while "on an adjusted basis" the company reported "net income of $36 million, or $0.79 per diluted share" and "adjusted EBITDA for the quarter was $72.7 million." (Senior VP, CFO & Treasurer Scott Zuehlke)

Outlook

  • "For modeling purposes... we expect revenue growth of 2% to 3% and adjusted EBITDA margin expansion of 50 to 75 basis points" and "we believe an estimated tax rate of approximately 24% should be reasonable for the fourth quarter of 2026." (Senior VP, CFO & Treasurer Zuehlke)
  • "We continue to believe we will exit 2026 with an even lower net leverage ratio as we continue to generate cash and repay debt." (Senior VP, CFO & Treasurer Zuehlke)
  • "Any further change in this dynamic will require additional discussions with our customers or additional surcharges to protect margins." (President, CEO & Chairman Wilson)

Financial Results

  • "The increase was mainly due to favorable impacts from pricing, partially offset by the impact of IEEPA tariff reimbursements to customers" and "we estimate the volumes were flat, pricing was up about 3%, and the negative tariff refund impact was approximately 2%." (Senior VP, CFO & Treasurer Zuehlke)
  • "We generated sufficient cash to repay $42.25 million of debt" and "we also repurchased $1.7 million of our stock" while "free cash flow increased by 3.5% to $47.8 million" and "our leverage ratio of net debt to last 12 months adjusted EBITDA decreased to 2.8x." (Senior VP, CFO & Treasurer Zuehlke)
  • "Adjusted EBITDA was $27.1 million" in Hardware Solutions, "adjusted EBITDA declined slightly to $35.6 million" in Extruded Solutions, and "adjusted EBITDA declined to $12 million" in Custom Solutions, with management attributing the segment pressure primarily to "general inflationary pressures" and "inflationary pressures we have already discussed." (Senior VP, CFO & Treasurer Zuehlke)

Q&A

  • Julio Romero, Sidoti & Company, LLC: "how much of the announced price increases were realized and how much of the benefit is there to come in the fourth quarter?" Senior VP, CFO & Treasurer Zuehlke: "the price increases we implemented in third quarter were phased so that we do expect... full impact in the fourth quarter of this year" and "price improved by about $3.1 million of the increase" in Hardware Solutions adjusted EBITDA.
  • Julio Romero, Sidoti & Company, LLC: "can you speak to the 80-20 benefit in the quarter" for Hardware? President, CEO & Chairman Wilson: "the benefits are minimal versus prior year because they're just now starting" and "I think you'll see those continue to pick up in the fourth quarter, and then in the next year you'll see more meaningful benefits."
  • Adam Thalhimer, Thompson, Davis & Company: asked about Q4 margin expansion and where to model it; Senior VP, CFO & Treasurer Zuehlke: "I would focus more on the Hardware Solutions segment" because "we still had a pretty big impact from the Monterrey issues that shouldn't be there this year." President, CEO & Chairman Wilson: "you're obviously going to get the full benefit of a full quarter's worth of the pricing impact."
  • Adam Thalhimer, Thompson, Davis & Company: asked about Wood Solutions growth drivers and outlook; Senior VP, CFO & Treasurer Zuehlke: "we were... able to win some new business... to the tune of like $10 million a year." President, CEO & Chairman Wilson: "the quoting activity is significantly picked up" and "we're actively quoting" on potential tariff-driven sourcing shifts.
  • Steven Ramsey, Thompson Research Group: asked about spacers demand/pricing and mix impact; President, CEO & Chairman Wilson: "the warm edge spacer markets are are very much tied to high-end energy-efficient windows" and "we have pricing mechanisms in place to protect us from inflationary pressures." Senior VP, CFO & Treasurer Zuehlke: "Those two product lines make up... like 65% to 70% revenue of that segment."
  • John McLeod (for Reuben Garner), StoneX: asked about tariff refunds/pass-through strategy; President, CEO & Chairman Wilson: "our philosophy has been we are not trying to use tariffs as a margin-generating item" and "if we get refunds, we'll pass it directly back to the customer."

Sentiment Analysis

  • Analysts: slightly positive, pressing on the durability and drivers of Q4 margin expansion and segment puts/takes, including "your margin guidance for Q4 struck me as particularly impressive" and requests for decomposition like "how does the growth break down" and "can you talk about the mix impact." (Adam Thalhimer; Steven Ramsey)
  • Management: slightly positive in prepared remarks and generally confident in mitigation actions, emphasizing "we have executed on that plan" and "we believe we have meaningfully narrowed the cost price gap," while also flagging conditionality with "any further change... will require additional discussions" and calling tariffs "fluid" and that "every day is different." (President, CEO & Chairman Wilson)
  • Versus prior quarter: management maintained caution on near-term macro conditions (Q2: "we remain cautious"; Q3: "the data has been mixed"), but the Q3 discussion carried more emphasis on realized actions and near-term cadence (Q3: "we expect revenue growth of 2% to 3%"), compared with Q2’s reduced visibility (Q2: "we are not reaffirming our previously issued guidance for fiscal 2026 at this time.") (Senior VP, CFO & Treasurer Zuehlke)

Quarter-over-Quarter Comparison

  • Guidance posture shifted from Q2’s pullback on full-year framing ("we are not reaffirming our previously issued guidance for fiscal 2026 at this time") to Q3 providing a specific Q4 cadence ("we expect revenue growth of 2% to 3% and adjusted EBITDA margin expansion of 50 to 75 basis points"). (Senior VP, CFO & Treasurer Zuehlke)
  • Inflation and pricing narrative evolved from Q2 emphasizing rapid cost spikes and planned actions ("sharp increases in raw materials and logistics costs" and price increases "to be phased in throughout Q3") to Q3 emphasizing execution and phasing benefits into Q4 ("we have executed on that plan" and "we do expect... full impact in the fourth quarter"). (President, CEO & Chairman Wilson; Senior VP, CFO & Treasurer Zuehlke)
  • Analyst focus shifted from Q2’s index-lag mechanics and cash generation seasonality to Q3’s mix/margin durability (Hardware margin drivers, spacer mix, screens growth) and capital allocation trajectory (questioning net cash vs. M&A). (Steven Ramsey; Adam Thalhimer; Kevin Gainey)

Risks and Concerns

  • "Activity has been weaker than we anticipated" with specific concern that "single family starts" and "single-family completions" were down year-over-year, while "softness persists" in parts of Europe. (President, CEO & Chairman Wilson)
  • "Raw material, energy, freight, and logistic costs all remain elevated, and the disruption to international shipping routes continues to add both cost and lead time" with management adding, "We continue to monitor the situation in the Middle East, which is still having an impact on transportation costs and the price of raw materials and energy." (President, CEO & Chairman Wilson; Senior VP, CFO & Treasurer Zuehlke)
  • Tariff-related uncertainty remained active, with management describing tariff dynamics as "fluid" and noting they may drive customer sourcing changes that the company is "actively quoting" into. (President, CEO & Chairman Wilson)

Final Takeaway

Quanex management described a mixed housing backdrop with weaker-than-expected new construction, but pointed to permits and “demand deferred” as key underpinnings, while highlighting that targeted price increases were executed and are expected to show fuller benefit in Q4. Management’s near-term priorities remained centered on 80-20 optimization, footprint and cost actions, and cash generation used for debt reduction, alongside a Q4 modeling cadence calling for 2% to 3% revenue growth and 50 to 75 basis points of adjusted EBITDA margin expansion.

data.title: SA Asks: How does the new Cybercab impact Tesla?
data.description:
After market close on Thursday, Tesla unveiled its long-awaited Cybercab driverless robotaxi at an event in Austin, Texas.

We asked Seeking Alpha analysts Geneva Investor, Deep Value Investing, The Techie, and James Foord how they think the new robotaxi will impact Elon Musk's flagship company. 

Geneva Investor: I think the Cybercab confirms Tesla's (TSLA) long-term cost advantage without changing its 2027 outlook. The vehicle should cost a fraction of what Alphabet's (GOOGL) (GOOG) Waymo pays for its robotaxis. In my view, this is because Tesla owns and produces both the software and the vehicle itself, while Waymo relies on third parties for its cars.

My problem with Tesla's (TSLA) Cybercab concerns regulation. Federal safety standards still assume a human is sitting behind a wheel. The exemption that Amazon's (AMZN) Zoox was recently granted caps vehicles at 2,500 a year, and the policy that would remove this ceiling remains only a proposal. By my own numbers, robotaxis contribute somewhere between 0.1% and 1.3% of Tesla's revenue next year.

Abroad I am more cautious still. Baidu (BIDU) and Pony AI (PONY) are already operating in China, and Europe has not yet cleared even a hands-off Level 2 system. Personally, I stay bullish on Tesla (TSLA) for its manufacturing position in physical AI, not because I expect meaningful robotaxi revenue any time soon.

Deep Value Investing: Let me put it this way. If you wanted to attend the Cybercab launch event, Tesla (TSLA) actually ran a sweepstakes for Robotaxi riders between August 17 and 23, with five winners getting access to the event. 

Five. Let me say it again. Five. Now you understand why I was so skeptical in my pre-launch coverage. 

In any case, the event wasn't even streamed on X, despite the fact that millions were waiting for it, and Elon didn't even bother to attend. I mean, what else is there really to say?

To me, the message is quite clear. The focus is on SpaceX (SPCX) and a potential acquisition of Tesla (TSLA) to shift the narrative from robotaxis to something else (data centers in space sounds exciting enough to me). 

Back to the launch event, Cybercab rides are now available only in limited parts of Austin. The fleet looks relatively small, with 45 registered Cybercabs as of Friday morning versus Tesla's total of 420 registered autonomous vehicles in the state, let alone Waymo's 988 vehicles. As expected, no specific details on costs per operating mile or any deployment milestones. 

My big takeaway was Elon skipping the event and not streaming it on X. That tells me that Tesla's (TSLA) future is SpaceX (SPCX).

The Techie: For me, the new Cybercab signals that Tesla (TSLA) is slowly but surely beginning to act like the company the market is valuing it as, giving legs to what (forward-looking) should be a higher-margin recurring revenue base from Cybercab fleets. 

It’s no longer about gaining the lead in the market. The boat has already sailed on this after Waymo’s (GOOG) (GOOGL) scale lead in the U.S. and China’s lead almost everywhere else. Now, it’s about being best positioned to monetize a new era of ride-hailing, and despite lagging competitors, I still think that’s Tesla (TSLA). The company has the best, in my opinion, cost-per-mile structure, which is a result of the fact that it manufactures the vehicle at much lower operating costs and doesn’t need a middleman. 

I still don’t view this as an overnight story, and regulation is already proving to be tough, but I believe Tesla (TSLA) has all the tools to make this work with some trial and error.

James Foord: The Cybercab launch marks a make-or-break moment for Tesla (TSLA). While competitors like Google's (GOOG) (GOOGL) Waymo have been operating for some time now, Tesla could take the ride-sharing market by storm thanks to its manufacturing advantage and even an "owner network," meaning Tesla owners could potentially offer their personal cars to the ride-sharing network. 

Success in this industry could allow Tesla (TSLA) to enter a new stage of growth and finally grow into its lofty valuation. This is a massive opportunity, but now that the moment is here, management can no longer hide behind ambitious plans and intentions. Musk has to actually deliver now.

(James Foord is also leader of the SA investing group The Pragmatic Investor.)
